items.title: Reggie Watkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, May 22, 2018

ctx.x: But he would go to India once a year for several months to an Ashram of a guy named Sai Baba. They called him Sri Sathya Sai Baba and he was a spiritual leader. Maynard loved Sai Baba. He would go there, you know as he would say, once a year for six weeks or two months where it would be a cultural exchange. He would teach music, jazz, and then he would learn Indian music. He loved Indian music. So “Chala Nata” was a product of him wanting to have something in the repertoire — and that’s not the only thing, there…
That’s what I was trying to sing.
